aKLntZcp27M.title: RustConf 2018 - Closing Keynote - Using Rust For Game Development by Catherine West
aKLntZcp27M.summary: Catherine West's RustConf 2018 closing keynote on building a game in Rust and organizing a large codebase. It builds up an entity component system and generational indices step by step.
aKLntZcp27M.why: HN treats it as the go-to explanation of ECS, valuable even for people who don't use Rust.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: is still my favorite ECS explanation, because she builds the concept piece by piece starting from megaclass-hell to full entities-as-IDs with reasons for each step.

DlTq8DbRs4k.title: The UK's Failed Experiment in Rail Privatization
DlTq8DbRs4k.summary: Wendover Productions explains how UK rail privatization worked and why it failed. It covers the fragmented operator and infrastructure structure and why market forces apply poorly to rail.
DlTq8DbRs4k.why: Recommended in privatization and rail threads as a clear, well-sourced explanation of the UK rail mess.

quote.text: the people on the Wendover YouTube channel did a video on this back in March which explained the issue really well.

wOmjnioNulo.title: The Secret Reason Horses Let Us Ride Them
wOmjnioNulo.summary: CGP Grey explains why horses could be ridden and why other animals like zebras and bears were never domesticated for war or riding. It is a follow-up on the topic of animal domestication.
wOmjnioNulo.why: HN recommends it as a classic on why some animals are suited to farming and domestication and others are not.

quote.text: CGP Grey has a great video [0] that goes into why some animals are better to farm/breed/eat than others.

4q1dgn_C0AU.title: The surprising science of happiness | Dan Gilbert
4q1dgn_C0AU.summary: Psychologist Dan Gilbert argues in this TED talk that our psychological immune system lets us become happy even when things do not go as planned. He challenges the idea that we will be miserable if we do not get what we want.
4q1dgn_C0AU.why: HN cites it as one of the best TED talks and as evidence that people adapt to and come to like outcomes they cannot change.

quote.text: is one of the best TED talks of all time

A2zKARkpDW4.title: Boards of Canada - Dayvan Cowboy
A2zKARkpDW4.summary: The official video for Boards of Canada's Dayvan Cowboy, built from reassembled documentary footage. It forms a dreamlike journey from space to the sea and shore, including Kittinger's 1960 high-altitude jump and surfing footage.
A2zKARkpDW4.why: HN mentions it as a favorite ambient track and as a nicely edited tribute to Kittinger's jump.

quote.text: you can watch nicely edited footage of Kittinger's 1960 record of 100,000 feet

PC2JOQ7z5L0.title: What Happens After the Universe Ends?
PC2JOQ7z5L0.summary: PBS Space Time explains Roger Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology, in which the far future of our universe becomes the big bang of the next. It explores what could come after the universe ends.
PC2JOQ7z5L0.why: HN recommends it as a clearer explanation of Penrose's cyclic cosmology than comment threads can give.

quote.text: It's explained in this PBS Space Time episode much better

p3lsYlod5OU.title: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325
p3lsYlod5OU.summary: Lex Fridman talks with Tufts biologist Michael Levin about bioelectricity, embryogenesis, xenobots and how cells collectively pursue goals. They range into cognition, evolution and the possibility of aliens.
p3lsYlod5OU.why: HN links it as a long-form entry point to Levin's ideas on cancer, bioelectric signaling and intelligence beyond the brain, though one commenter finds some claims outlandish.

quote.text: here he goes over much of the same amazing material, but along with a visual presentation.

taaEzHI9xyY.title: Crockford on JavaScript - Section 8: Programming Style & Your Brain
taaEzHI9xyY.summary: Douglas Crockford's YUIConf 2011 keynote on why programming style matters, particularly in JavaScript. He draws on science about the brain and shows how tools like JSLint help.
taaEzHI9xyY.why: HN points to it as an entertaining, insightful talk about the nature of programming, with memorable lines about programmers and a refreshing slide style.

AAsICMPwGPY.title: Klein Bottles - Numberphile
AAsICMPwGPY.summary: Numberphile interviews Cliff Stoll about Klein bottles, the one-sided surfaces with no inside or outside. Stoll explains them with characteristic enthusiasm and shows off his collection.
AAsICMPwGPY.why: HN likes it for Cliff Stoll's infectious passion for topology, and it gets linked in threads about him and about Mobius strips.

quote.text: This guys passion for Mobius Strips is infectious.

WOHPuY88Ry4.title: Johnny Cash - A Boy Named Sue (Live at San Quentin, 1969)
WOHPuY88Ry4.summary: Johnny Cash's live performance of A Boy Named Sue at San Quentin in 1969, a comic country song about a man named Sue seeking revenge on his father.
WOHPuY88Ry4.why: Mostly invoked as a reference or joke in threads about names, the .su domain or hardship, rather than recommended.

dkZFtimgAcM.title: Douglas Crockford: Monads and Gonads (YUIConf Evening Keynote)
dkZFtimgAcM.summary: Douglas Crockford's YUIConf 2012 evening keynote tries to explain monads in a way programmers can actually understand, in the context of JavaScript. He aims to break the 'monad tutorial curse'.
dkZFtimgAcM.why: Mentioned as a great talk alongside Crockford's book, and mostly quoted for his quip that once you understand monads you lose the ability to explain them.

quote.text: The Monads and Gonads talk [0] he gave is also great.

1X7fZoDs9KU.title: Which country does the most good for the world? | Simon Anholt
1X7fZoDs9KU.summary: Policy advisor Simon Anholt presents the Good Country Index, a measure of how much each nation contributes to the world beyond its own borders. In a funny TED talk he argues governments should think globally, and reveals which countries rank surprisingly.
1X7fZoDs9KU.why: HN points to it as an alternative to GDP for measuring national progress and as background on the Good Country Index.

quote.text: Maybe this is a better way of measuring progress instead of GDP and productivity?

6WGKz2sUa0w.title: Why all solar panels are secretly LEDs (and all LEDs are secretly solar panels)
6WGKz2sUa0w.summary: Steve Mould shows that LEDs and solar panels are both diodes made from semiconductors, so a solar panel can emit light and an LED can generate electricity. He demonstrates a small solar panel lighting up.
6WGKz2sUa0w.why: Cited as a neat demonstration that diodes work in both directions in semiconductor and LED discussions.

quote.text: Steve Mould had a video[1] about this a couple of years ago where he shows a small solar panel lighting up.

85OysZ_4lp0.title: 2015 Nissan Tsuru vs. 2016 Nissan Versa
85OysZ_4lp0.summary: An IIHS car-to-car crash test pitting a 2015 Nissan Tsuru, sold in Mexico, against a 2016 Nissan Versa, sold in the US. It is a 40 mph, 50 percent overlap collision that shows how safety standards differ between markets.
85OysZ_4lp0.why: Cited as a stark demonstration of how much car safety has improved and how regulation differs between countries.

quote.text: Here's a crash test between a 2015 Nissan Tsuru, the least expensive sedan sold by Nissan in Mexico, and a 2016 Nissan Versa

ErpNpR3XYUw.title: Google Glass
ErpNpR3XYUw.summary: A short 2012 promotional-style video of Google Glass showing what the headset was meant to do. It shows features like map directions and overlays in the wearer's view.
ErpNpR3XYUw.why: Cited as an example of what Glass promised, for comparison with later AR glasses.

HaF-nRS_CWM.title: Winamp 2.91 -- It Really Whips the Llama's Ass
HaF-nRS_CWM.summary: A brief clip of the Winamp 2.91 startup sound, with its famous audio line about whipping the llama's ass, uploaded as a tribute.
HaF-nRS_CWM.why: HN commenters post it as a nostalgic joke or pun in Winamp threads, and sometimes for the classic startup audio.

msXtgTVMcuA.title: SPRINT ABM - Zero to Mach 10 in 5 Seconds!
msXtgTVMcuA.summary: A short clip of the Sprint anti-ballistic missile, which was launched from a silo and reached Mach 10 within seconds. Its nose and skin glow white hot from aerodynamic heating.
msXtgTVMcuA.why: HN links it as striking footage of how fast and heat-stressed hypersonic interceptors and ICBM re-entry vehicles are.

quote.text: Here is a US missile maneuvering at mach 10 to intercept a RV going at mach 30. In 1972.

ue7wM0QC5LE.title: Four Yorkshiremen- Monty Python
ue7wM0QC5LE.summary: The classic Monty Python sketch in which four Yorkshiremen compete to claim the hardest upbringing, each story more absurd than the last.
ue7wM0QC5LE.why: Quoted as a joke whenever commenters one-up each other on past hardships.
